clue.text: No time!

parts.note: no amount at all is nought, the figure 0
an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A frantic cry that there is not a moment to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'No' gives the nought word and 'time' the sixty-minute unit, and together they name the moment an operation begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The appointed starting moment of a military attack is counted from nought, so it is the 'nothing' hour.

clue.text: Signs the last letter — flip ping do one across!

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: flipping turns the word do over so it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
AC is a standard abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: An exasperated order to do the first across clue, flipping well get on with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive in the surface, but it is the reversal signal; 'the last letter' means of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the band of twelve astrological star signs.

clue.text: Discover case of remarkable beef

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of remarkable are kept

parts.note: veal is the meat of a calf, loosely counted as beef

explanation.surface: A diner finds a notable box of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something hidden is to uncover or disclose it.

clue.text: Checked with Henry and Edward

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Ted is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: Something was inspected in the company of two men called Henry and Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked in the sense of stopped or brought to a standstill.

clue.text: The aristocracy don't start dinner with leftover bread

indicators.note: not starting means the evening meal word loses its opening letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal, a dinner
a crust is the hard end piece of bread often left uneaten

explanation.surface: Snobbish nobles refuse to begin a meal containing stale bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start' takes S off SUPPER to leave UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper crust is an idiom for the highest social class.

clue.text: Agrees to ring before Sunday

parts.note: to chime is to ring like a bell

explanation.surface: Someone consents to telephone before the weekend is out.
explanation.definitionFit: When one thing chimes with another the two harmonise or are in accord.

clue.text: In the spring term, it causes amusement

indicators.note: In tells us the word it sits inside the name of the term

parts.note: Hilary is the name of the spring term at Oxford and some other British institutions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about what makes people laugh during the spring term at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the name Oxford and Trinity College Dublin give to the term starting in January; 'In' looks like a link word but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud merriment and laughter.

clue.text: The devilry that is found in motorway's controller

indicators.note: found in signals the little word sitting inside the other pieces

parts.note: M is a British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
a chief is one in charge, a controller
taken as written

explanation.surface: The source of wickedness turns out to be the person who runs the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are named by M plus a number, as in the M1, so 'motorway' gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful naughtiness, a kind of devilment.

clue.text: The odds on impostor's dog

parts.note: SP stands for starting price, the betting odds on a racehorse at the off
a ringer is an impostor, especially a horse entered under a false identity

explanation.surface: A punter's thoughts on a race involving a fake contestant's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from horse racing: SP for starting price and RINGER for a substitute horse running under another's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a breed of spaniel, a gundog.

clue.text: Grows love sick -hurried back outside

indicators.note: outside says the reversed word goes round the rearranged letters
back means the word for hurried is read in the other direction

parts.note: sped is a past form of speed, to hurry

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters of love are unwell and out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovesick person hurries home and matures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SPED into DEPS, and 'sick' rearranges LOVE into VELO; DEPS goes 'outside' VELO.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to expand or mature, as a child does.

clue.text: A bit more stuffy about one who never wins

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
a loser is someone who fails to win

explanation.surface: A remark about a hapless competitor's slightly airless surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and airless, so closer means more oppressive.

clue.text: Sportsmen who are a must in fashion

indicators.note: in fashion read as being fashioned or reshaped, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashionable sports players regard something as essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' looks like it means trendy but reshapes ARE A MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs are players who compete without being paid.

clue.text: Child in street found a star fish, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a ragged child living on the streets
a spiny sea creature related to the starfish

explanation.definitionFit: A street urchin is a scruffy child, and a sea urchin is a spiny echinoderm, cousin to the starfish.

clue.text: His agents live for conversion!

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A preacher's agents exist to win over new believers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a preacher whose helpers live to convert others.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist preaches the gospel to win converts.

clue.text: Look after soldier's magazine

indicators.note: after puts the looking word behind the soldier

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch over an army man's munitions store.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIVATE EYE is a long-running British satirical magazine; 'magazine' in the surface suggests a weapons store.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye is the title of a fortnightly British satirical publication.

clue.text: A useful-sounding lid for hamper

indicators.note: sounding means the word for useful is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: handy means useful
a cap is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: A practical cover for a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'useful-sounding' gives HANDI, said like HANDY; 'hamper' looks like a basket but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap is to hinder or impede, as to hamper is.

clue.text: Fair point, accepted by total being altered

indicators.note: accepted by means the first pieces are taken inside the word for total

parts.note: to add is to total up
just means fair
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A fair point is taken on board and the sum is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' is the container signal; 'point' means a compass point, the usual crossword source of E, N, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted means modified slightly or changed to fit.

clue.text: Skilfully manufactured cheese turned up after spring

indicators.note: after puts the reversed cheese behind the spring

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the cheese is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Fine cheese appears after the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses because this is a down clue, read upwards; 'spring' looks like the season but is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-made describes something soundly constructed with skill.

clue.text: Speaking to a deputy head before lining up

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: dressing is the military term for lining up troops in straight ranks

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses a deputy headteacher before assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: In drill, to dress ranks is to align them, so lining up is DRESSING.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them directly.

clue.text: Iron bar lifted a lid

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the bar word goes upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: An iron bar is used to prise up a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses because this is a down clue; 'lid' is informal slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat, and lid is slang for a hat.

clue.text: Speak unfavourably of African country dancing's last new leader

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the dancing word
leader picks the opening letter of new

explanation.surface: A report on the latest leader to emerge in an African nation known for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign is to slander or disparage.

clue.text: Stage conclusion to story

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Reaching the final phase of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale or myth.

clue.text: It may precede each of Dutch entry standards

definitions.text: It may precede each of Dutch entry standards

parts.words: It may precede each of Dutch entry standards
parts.note: one word can go before each of Dutch, entry and standards to make three familiar phrases: nonsense talk, a bookkeeping system and hypocrisy

explanation.surface: Something comes before Dutch rules on admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubled Dutch is gibberish, the doubled entry method is bookkeeping, and doubled standards means hypocrisy: the same twofold word fronts each.

clue.text: Enjoy getting back with plenty of time for purchase

indicators.note: getting back means the enjoying word is turned round

parts.note: to revel in something is to enjoy it
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys returning with time to spare for some shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' turns REVEL into LEVER; 'purchase' means grip, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage and purchase both mean the mechanical grip or advantage used to move something.

clue.text: Sleep better, embracing revolutionary worker

indicators.note: embracing means the first word holds the reversed second inside it

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the insect is read backwards

parts.note: a worker is an ant, the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A political radical's labourer is better off asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like an adjective for the worker but signals turning it round, and 'embracing' puts that inside the word meaning to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light doze.

clue.text: Dealing in ice, not in poi son

indicators.note: dealing as with cards, distributing the letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trafficking in drugs, though not in poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealing' rearranges ICE NOT IN; 'ice' looks like drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the toxic alkaloid found in tobacco.

clue.text: Sky pilots who are spared at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Aviators who were saved when they came down over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky pilots' is slang for clergy, not aviators.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is old slang for a chaplain or clergyman, and padres are military chaplains.

clue.text: Soldier's leader is disciplined but under stress

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: trained means drilled or disciplined

explanation.surface: An army officer is well drilled yet feeling the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Strained means tense or under pressure.
